key_insight: A repeatable, evidence-based evaluation pipeline can identify which LLM prompt templates produce personalized, pedagogically aligned follow‑up questions in structured educational dialogues, demonstrated by testing six prompt templates.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of systematic methods for designing and evaluating prompts that reliably generate personalized and educationally appropriate outputs for learning applications.
method: Design a set of six prompt templates targeted at generating follow‑up questions within a structured dialogue activity.
Use LLM(s) to produce responses from each template and collect generated follow‑up questions across conditions.
Evaluate outputs with a mix of pedagogical/persona rubrics and quality metrics (e.g., alignment, personalization, relevance), using human raters and/or automated measures to compare templates.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and EdTech designers a practical framework to iterate on prompt design and select templates that better support personalized learning and pedagogical goals, reducing trial-and-error deployment risk.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the evaluation pipeline: prompt templates → LLM generation → annotation/metrics → comparison
Bar or radar chart comparing templates across key metrics (pedagogical alignment, personalization, relevance, coherence)
Example dialogue panel showing a student prompt and contrasting follow‑up questions from high- vs low-performing templates
Icon set: template (document), LLM (neural/brain), rubric (checklist), pedagogy (graduation cap)
paper_title: LLM Prompt Evaluation for Educational Applications
paper_authors: Langdon Holmes, Adam Coscia, Scott Crossley, Joon Suh Choi, Wesley Morris
